findings.issue: 200 is read digit-by-digit as にれいれい. In Japanese, 200ドル is read にひゃくドル (nihyaku-doru); にれいれい is not a valid reading of the amount 200.
findings.current: わたしにとってにれいれいどるわたいきんです。
findings.suggested: わたしにとってにひゃくどるわたいきんです。

findings.issue: Reading of numeral token 200 is wrong: にれいれい is digit-by-digit spelling, not the actual reading of the quantity 200, which is にひゃく.
Romaji carries the same wrong reading of 200: 'nireirei' instead of 'nihyaku'.
English gloss of 暖かく says 'hot', but 暖かい means 'warm' (pleasantly warm); 'hot' is 暑い. The pt gloss ('ameno / agradavelmente quente') is correct, so en and pt are also inconsistent.

Token list starts with two stray tokens 外国(がいこく) and 人(じん) with all-null glosses, placed BEFORE 私. They duplicate the correct 外国人 token that appears later in proper position; reconstructing the sentence from tokens yields corrupted text.
findings.current: leading stray tokens: 外国(がいこく), 人(じん) before 私
findings.suggested: delete the two stray tokens 外国 and 人; keep only the full 外国人(がいこくじん) token in its correct position

findings.issue: Garbled English: missing the word 'marked' ('is by が') and a misplaced opening parenthesis swallows the rest of the paragraph. The pt version is well-formed; the en should match it.
findings.current: is by が (〜が必要だ treats the object of need as the grammatical subject. Predicate 必要である is the literary/written form of 必要だ.)
findings.suggested: is marked by が: 〜が必要だ treats the object of need as the grammatical subject. The predicate 必要である is the literary/written form of 必要だ.

findings.issue: 子供 is gender-neutral 'child'; glossing it as 'son' first over-specifies (son = 息子). The natural en translation itself uses 'child'.
lit_en renders 子供 as 'my son', over-specifying gender relative to the Japanese and inconsistent with the natural en translation 'my child'.
findings.current: As for my son, whatever it is, he wants to know it.
findings.suggested: As for my child, whatever it is, they want to know it.
